theme: 3 terms on translating an app: the per-language strings file, the lookup function, and the single catalog file

terms.definition: A file that lists keys and their translated text, one file for each language.
terms.example: Add the new button text to Localizable Strings for Korean.
terms.code:
let text = Bundle.main.localizedString(
    forKey: "welcome",
    value: nil,
    table: "Localizable")
print(text)

terms.definition: A function that looks up the translated text for a key.
terms.example: Use NSLocalizedString so the title changes with the user's language.
terms.code:
let title = NSLocalizedString(
    "welcome",
    comment: "Greeting on home")
print(title)

terms.definition: A single Xcode file that holds all your translations and shows which ones are missing.
terms.example: Move our old strings files into a String Catalog to see every missing translation.
terms.code:
let text = String(
    localized: "welcome",
    table: "Localizable")
print(text)

Learn to explain how to translate an iOS app: Localizable Strings, NSLocalizedString & String Catalog, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Localizable Strings - A file that lists keys and their translated text, one file for each language.
NSLocalizedString - A function that looks up the translated text for a key.
String Catalog - A single Xcode file that holds all your translations and shows which ones are missing.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Localizable Strings, NSLocalizedString and String Catalog in English?

dialogue.title: Missing Korean text

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the Korean build still shows English on the home screen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you wrap the text in NSLocalizedString?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, the key is `welcome`, like in the code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then check Localizable Strings. Does the Korean file have that key?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. I only added it to the English one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add it there. Or move everything to a String Catalog.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is a String Catalog really better?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. It is one file, and it shows every missing translation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. And what about the `comment` text?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It helps translators. Always write a clear `comment` in NSLocalizedString.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. I will fix Localizable Strings first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sounds good. Then migrate to a String Catalog after the release.
